title: Make Ctrl+Backspace send 0x08 for previous-word delete
body:
Foreman sends Ctrl+Backspace as plain Backspace (0x7f), dropping Ctrl. Windows Terminal sends 0x08 (^H) for Ctrl+Backspace, and many TUIs and shells (PSReadLine, some readline/zsh configs, agent CLIs) bind ^H to backward-kill-word, so Windows users expect Ctrl+Backspace to delete the previous word.

Start in src/input.rs: encode_key's Key::Backspace arms. Alt+Backspace already sends ESC 0x7f (card d68wo1).

Decide before coding:
- Ctrl+Alt+Backspace: keep 0x7f or send ESC 0x08? AltGr arrives as Ctrl+Alt on Windows, so be conservative.
- Risk: apps that treat 0x08 as a plain backspace (not word-delete) will see Ctrl+Backspace act like Backspace. That's fine; it matches Windows Terminal.

Done when: encode_key unit test + process_input test for Ctrl+Backspace -> [0x08], and a live check (foreman send/snapshot) that it deletes a word in PowerShell/PSReadLine and in Claude Code.
